value.body: An animator brings drawings and models to life by creating movement, frame by frame or with digital rigs. Animation and VFX studios, game studios, ad agencies and e-learning companies hire animators. A typical day involves working on assigned shots, presenting them at reviews and making revisions.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BFA (Applied Art / Animation), B.Des or an animation diploma

items.label: Key hiring factor
items.value: A showreel of your own work

items.label: Animation & VFX segment revenue (India)
items.note: Segment of the media and entertainment sector; FICCI-EY-based estimates differ slightly by definition
items.source: PIB backgrounder 'Creative Industries as Growth Engines' (16 Feb 2026)

items.label: AVGC professionals needed (projection)
items.note: A projection for animation, VFX, gaming, comics and XR combined, not a count of current jobs
items.source: PIB backgrounder 'Creative Industries as Growth Engines' (16 Feb 2026), as stated

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers are hired mainly on a showreel. Many start as trainee or junior animators, or in related studio roles such as in-betweening or clean-up, and move up shot by shot. Studio tests are common.

value.title: At a glance
items: Common next roles: senior animator, lead animator, animation supervisor.
Much studio work is project-based, so workload rises and falls.
Software changes, so ongoing practice and learning are part of the job.

competition.note: BFA graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
competition.source: AISHE 2023-24, Table 34 (programme-wise out-turn), Ministry of Education
